work_packages.name: From any engine checkout, one command builds and tests a game in a games repository against that checkout
work_packages.quality_bar: The relationship Bevy, Godot and Fyrox have with the games built on them, kept honest by a gate in the manner of rust-lang's crater: the engine is checked alone, and a game is checked against the exact engine commit in question.

items.statement: `python3 scripts/game_gate.py <game> <command>` finds the games repository beside the main checkout, or only where `THRUM_GAMES` says when that is set, builds the named game against the engine checkout the command runs in, and runs the game's command. A game whose manifests name `../../thrum/crates/…` builds against a builder's worktree with no change to the game.
items.ask: Read the test. Does it make a scratch games repository and two engine trees that differ, and show the game built against the tree the gate ran in and not the sibling one? Does it pass with no `thrum-games` on the machine?

items.statement: The gate never writes into the games repository, refuses a games tree with uncommitted changes unless told to take it as it stands, and its record names both revisions, the engine's and the game's.
items.ask: After a gate run, is the games repository's working tree, lockfile and index exactly as before? What does the record hold when the games tree was taken as it stands?

items.statement: With no games repository the gate says so and exits with a code of its own. `./dev check` needs no games repository and never calls the gate. The in-tree game is still built by `./dev check` until WP4.
items.ask: Is the exit code for a missing repository distinct from a failed build and from a failed game check? With `THRUM_GAMES` set to a path that does not exist, does the gate report a missing repository even when one sits beside the main checkout? Does anything in `./dev check` call the gate?

items.statement: `boundary` runs the shape rules on a game: its only path dependencies are packages under the engine's `crates/`, no source file or build script reaches outside the game except through them, and it has neither engine test package as a normal dependency.
items.ask: Does the test's scratch game fail `boundary` when it depends on a package under the engine's `examples/`, when it includes a file from the engine's source by path, and when it takes `thrum-fixtures` as a normal dependency?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this work package moved no retained image.

work_packages.name: No engine crate reaches into a game or an example, and the engine's tests build with the games taken away
work_packages.quality_bar: The line Bevy and wgpu hold between their crates and their examples: examples depend on the engine, never the other way, by any route a compiler can follow.

items.statement: `package-reach` is at zero for the whole repository: no source file includes another package's files, and no package under `crates/` depends on one under `examples/` in any way.

The mixed-mesh field is defined once, as plain data in `crates/thrum-fixtures`, which depends on nothing. `thrum-render`'s visibility tests read it as a dev-dependency and the proving ground reads it as a normal dependency, in its Mac and its wasm32 build. `test-crate-edges` is at zero.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule test-crate-edges --zero . && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-render --test visibility_buckets && cargo build --locked --offline -p v1-game --lib && ./dev check-web'
items.ask: Is the field's data (entities, materials, camera path, prop meshes, day cycle) defined anywhere but `thrum-fixtures`: in the proving ground, in `thrum-render`'s tests, or as a second copy? Does `thrum-fixtures` depend on wgpu or on any workspace package? Does anything but the proving ground take it as a normal dependency? Are the visibility tests' assertions and references unedited?

items.statement: The temporal witness and the cloud shader source are reached through `thrum-render`'s public API, by `thrum-asset-gpu`, the proving ground and the web build alike.
items.ask: Does any engine test's result still depend on a file under `examples/`? Does the web build script still copy a file out of `thrum-render`'s source?

items.statement: Every package under `crates/` builds its tests with `examples/v1-game` and `examples/v1-game-ios` absent from the tree.
items.ask: Read the script. Does it work on a copy in which the two folders are really absent, and build tests and benches, not only libraries?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this work package moved no retained image.

work_packages.name: The game builds and passes its own tests with every engine rig compiled out, and a normal build ships no test hooks
work_packages.quality_bar: A game that could be lifted out of the repository today: what Godot's demo projects are to Godot, with the engine's own test rigs kept on the engine's side of a line a compiler enforces.

items.statement: `examples/v1-game` has a `proving` feature, on by default, that holds every engine rig, selection and qualification export. With it off the package builds for the Mac and for wasm32, and the game's own tests pass.
items.check: sh -c 'cargo test --locked --offline -p v1-game --no-default-features --test game_alone && cargo build --locked --offline -p v1-game --no-default-features --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown'
items.ask: With the feature off, does the library export anything that qualifies an engine module? Which tests are the game's own, and do they all run with it off? Is any test target declared with `required-features`, which would let another module's check pass by running nothing?

items.statement: Rigs that need no hosted scene live with the code they test: the cooked texture quality and staging-fault tests are `thrum-asset-gpu`'s.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-asset-gpu --features fault-probe --test cooked_fault_gpu --test cooked_texture_quality

items.statement: A normal web build exports no qualification function and a normal iPhone build accepts no qualification command. The proving builds that other modules' checks run still have them.
items.ask: Which exports does the default web bundle hold? Do the browser and simulator checks that other modules pinned still find the hooks they drive, with their check strings unchanged?

items.statement: No file under `crates/` names a game: `game-names` refuses a game's package name, crate name or control key in engine source, and is at zero.
Every check that an open item in another module pins on `v1-game` still finds what it names, under the default features.
items.ask: Take the open items in other modules whose checks name `-p v1-game`: does each named test target that existed at the starting commit still exist and run with no extra flag?

findings.name: Exact-image verification records the wrong Wasm artifact hashes

work_packages.name: The showcase game lives in `thrum-games`, builds against the engine through its public API alone, and passes the V1 exit check from there
work_packages.quality_bar: The showcase as a real external consumer, as a studio's game is of Unreal or a Bevy game is of Bevy: it builds from its own repository against an engine it cannot reach into, and the exit it passed inside the engine's repository it passes again from outside.

items.statement: `/Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum-games` is a Git repository with no remote and one first commit: the V1 game as a copy with no history and no proving code, with its content, routes, presets, exit configuration, launcher and the exit baselines its checks compare with. Its packages reach the engine only by path to `../../thrum/crates/`.
items.ask: Does `git -C` the games repository show one root commit and no remote? Does its tree hold any rig, selection or qualification export of an engine module?

items.statement: The game builds and passes its own tests from there against the engine checkout under test, for the Mac and for wasm32.

The V1 exit's rows hold from outside. Through the gate, each of the three rows runs the six stops and the exit flythrough and reports what the exit configuration says; the rows agree with each other and with the exit baselines; the three controls fail as they must; and the Mac panel and the Chrome page declare the same controls, with the six presets applied on every row. The record names the engine and game revisions, and the V1 exit record gains a dated note of the run.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game check --exit && python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game exit --row mac-apple && python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game exit --row mac-portable && python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game exit --row chrome && python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game exit --compare && python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game exit --controls'
items.ask: Are these the commands `SHOWCASE` WP5.5 and WP7.2 to WP7.6 pinned, passed through the gate with their thresholds and baselines unchanged? Is the Chrome row a real browser run? Does the note in the exit record claim anything about looks or cadence, which this run did not judge?

items.statement: The V1 exit's live clauses hold from outside, on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome: the time controls scrub from dawn through night, a saved edit to a prop mesh and to the ground texture appears without a restart or a page reload, and the profiler's rows are current. The edited files are the game's own assets, in the tree the gate built from.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game exit --clauses --target mac-metal && python3 scripts/game_gate.py v1-game exit --clauses --target chrome-webgpu'
items.ask: Are these the commands `SHOWCASE` WP7.7 and WP7.8 pinned, unchanged in what they require? Which file does each edit change, and which folder does the game's watcher watch: would the clause fail if the watcher still pointed at Thrum's frozen copy under `examples/v1-game/assets`?

items.statement: Thrum holds nothing that is the game's. The launcher, the exit configuration and the exit baselines are in the games repository, with the game's own copies of the presets, routes and sources it uses, and `scripts/run_v1_showcase.py` forwards to the gate so recorded command lines still run. What stays at `examples/v1-game` is the engine's proving ground with the frozen qualification content: the scenes, presets, routes, valley sources and pages that the registered baselines and other modules' checks read, at the paths they read them. Its README and crate docs say so.
items.ask: What under `examples/`, `scripts/` or `docs/` in Thrum would a change to the showcase game still have to edit? Is every file the design lists as frozen qualification content still tracked in Thrum at its path? Does the proving ground's first page say that it is engine test content and where the game is?

items.statement: The repository guard knows that games live outside: `.config/architecture.toml` declares no game in this workspace and the guard refuses a package that declares itself one. README, AGENTS, REPOSITORY and `thrum-engineering` say where the game is, how to build it against a checkout, and that an engine work package proves itself in its own crate or the proving ground.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/repo_check.py && python3 scripts/test_repo_check.py && ! grep -q external_game .config/architecture.toml'
items.ask: Does the guard's self-test declare a game package in a scratch registry and see the guard refuse it?

items.statement: The engine qualifies itself with the games repository unavailable: every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit with `THRUM_GAMES` pointing at nothing, and the verifier hands that variable on to every command it starts. This work package moved no retained image, and the verifier reads no input from outside Thrum.
items.ask: The verifier starts its commands with `THRUM_` variables removed: does `THRUM_GAMES`, and no other, now reach them, so that a command which looked for the games repository in this run would have found none? Does the verifier, either native matrix, the Chrome capture or the web build read any file outside this repository, or call the gate? Is there any route but `THRUM_GAMES` and the gate by which a script in Thrum finds the games repository?

work_packages.name: The proving ground carries its own name, the game's iPhone app has followed the game, and nothing in Thrum is called a game
work_packages.quality_bar: A repository whose names tell the truth, as Bevy's `examples/` and `benches/` do: a newcomer never mistakes the engine's test content for a game.

items.statement: The package at `examples/v1-game` is renamed for what it is, in its folder, package name, crate docs, scripts and the baseline registry's covered paths, and every name an open item's check uses still works.
items.ask: Did the registry change anything but paths? Does any document a builder reads first still call the proving ground a game?

items.statement: The game's iPhone app is in the games repository, on the engine's shared shell, and passes its simulator checks through the gate.
items.ask: Is any iPhone code of the game's left in Thrum? Simulator results are function only: is anything else claimed?

items.statement: No package or folder under `crates/`, `examples/` or `tools/` is a game or is named for one, and a script names a game only to forward to the gate.
items.check: python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule game-names --zero crates examples tools
items.ask: Which scripts still name the V1 game, and does each only forward to the gate or record history?
